tier1.name: Policy Scenario Lab (PSL)
tier1.description: An agent based policy laboratory that compares candidate AI regulatory instruments on a synthetic AI economy: firms choosing capability, safety, compliance and location; a regulator; the public; the press; the market. Each instrument is scored on expected harm avoided against its economic and social cost, with the industry's net gain or loss, the forecast news environment and the market reaction reported beside it.
tier1.how_used: To inform, not to make, a policy choice: the briefing is drafted from the run's artefacts, checked by an independent critic and released by a named human at a second gate. Outputs are expected values with intervals on a declared set of assumptions; they are not forecasts of named companies or events.

senior_responsible_owner_register.source: dev mode (PSL_DEV_MODE=on); not a regulated person

owner_and_responsibility.external_supplier: none; the tool runs on the authority's own infrastructure

description_and_rationale.detailed_description: Monthly agent based simulation over 36 months on 60 Monte Carlo paths per instrument, on common random numbers; a welfare accounting of harm avoided, consumer surplus, output uplift, resident producer surplus, compliance resource cost, enforcement budget, offshore leakage, relocation cost and labour adjustment; a decision metric (expected net social value under the question's constraints) with a bootstrap for the probability that each instrument is best.
description_and_rationale.scope: Candidate AI regulatory instruments: Status quo (voluntary commitments), Compute threshold reporting, Coordinated frontier licensing, Frontier licensing, Six month moratorium above the threshold
description_and_rationale.benefit: A reproducible, assumption explicit comparison of instruments that no single study provides, with its uncertainty shown.
description_and_rationale.previous_process: Narrative impact assessments and expert elicitation without a common counterfactual.
description_and_rationale.alternatives_considered: Static cost benefit spreadsheets; econometric event studies alone; expert panels.

decision_making_process.process_integration: The policy question enters at the RUN page; the battery is approved at Gate 1; the briefing is released at Gate 2.
decision_making_process.provided_information: Preferred option Coordinated frontier licensing: expected net social value 18.8 $bn [-15.1, 10.7]; harm avoided 22.1 $bn; industry value change -129 $bn; P(best) 90%.
decision_making_process.frequency_and_scale: On demand per question; every run is kept in the registry.
decision_making_process.human_decisions_and_review: Two named human gates with refusal and recorded reasons; an independent critic before Gate 2; the briefing cites every assumption.
decision_making_process.required_training: Familiarity with cost benefit analysis and with the assumptions file.
decision_making_process.appeals_and_review: Any figure can be recomputed from the evidence pack by a second authority; the ledger is replayable.

tool_specification.system_architecture: Python; numpy; a Dash terminal; a hash chained HMAC signed ledger; a register of approvers.
tool_specification.maintenance: versioned; the code fingerprint of each run is recorded
tool_specification.models: No learned model in the decision path; an optional language model may phrase text and its output is vetted number by number.

data.source_data: Synthetic economy by default; optional uploaded price series for calibration and event studies, through a quarantine that refuses personal data.
data.data_sharing: The evidence pack carries only public or synthetic rows.

risks_mitigations_and_impact_assessments.impact_assessment: The tornado, structural variants and red team in assurance.json; the decision gap between early appearance and long run value.
risks: The harm side rests on declared hazard and tail assumptions; the tornado shows which change the answer.
The firms are archetypes; mapping onto real companies requires calibration and is labelled as such.
A domestic instrument can be escaped by relocation; the leakage term depends on the mobility assumed.
Expected values hide path dependence; the intervals and P(best) must be read with the means.
risks_mitigations_and_impact_assessments.mitigations: Every assumption is declared and bounded; common random numbers; an independent critic; two gates; a replayable ledger; the preferred option is reported with the assumptions that would change it.
